title: Compact debug sparkline prototypes
body: Purpose:\nThis note captures a light-weight, high-density wireframe + interaction proposal for surfacing and triaging error behaviors (timeouts, 5xx, model-level errors) in the Console error list without forcing users into a full trace explorer. Aim is to give engineers a fast signal->action loop for recurring or high-impact failure modes.
body_addendum:
Design constraints and assumptions:
- Primary user: engineer on-call or feature owner doing quick TTR (time-to-resolution) work.
- Console list view is busy; we want an at-a-glance heatmap for recent regressions and a tiny inline timeline for each route/session.
- Should be keyboard-friendly and cheap to render (SVG sparklines and simplified badges).
- Must link to deep-dive (existing failure replay) but default flow should allow patching a rule/rolldown from the list.
proposal_summary:
Core idea: compact sparkline + error fingerprint card per route/flow
- Each row in the error table includes a 48x12 sparkline showing failure rate over the last 48 hours (30m buckets).
- Overlaid on the sparkline are tiny markers for distinct error fingerprints (color-coded: red=5xx, orange=timeout, purple=model-error) with hover tooltips.
- A micro-metric stack to the left: instantaneous 95th latency, token-rate per second, and error percent as tiny numeric chips.
- Expand-in-place: pressing Enter or clicking mini-chevron expands a thin panel (max 160px height) that shows the top 3 sample traces, a short hypothesis line, and 2 quick-actions: "Reroute to fallback model" and "Create rollback/patch".
visual_notes:
Wireframe notes for the 1-row compact card: 
- Left: route name + model badge + small muted description (one-line).
- Mid: sparkline 48x12 with faint grid, black baseline = success, colored markers for fingerprint peaks. Hover shows time window and sample count.
- Right: chips: [err% 3.4%] [p95 320ms] [tokens/s 120] and an action kebab.
- Expand panel: two columns. Left column: 3 ranked trace snippets (timestamp, short error message, model-version, quantization-profile). Right column: small quick-fixes and triage checklist (assign, postmortem link, mark as transient).
ASCII mockup for row (compact):
[route-name] [m:rw-4] | ▁▁▂▃▅▂▁▁◉▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁ | [err% 4.2] [p95 420ms]  •  ⋮
Expand ->
-----------------------------------------
| sample 1 | 2026-02-26 11:12 | 504 gateway | model-v2-q4 | quick-action: reroute |
| sample 2 | 2026-02-26 10:58 | timeout 30s  | model-v2-q4 | quick-action: increase-timeout |
-----------------------------------------
interaction_patterns:
Micro-interactions and keyboard flows:
- Row focus with up/down arrows; Enter toggles expand; 'c' opens create-issue modal pre-populated with selected fingerprint and top traces.
- Hover on sparkline shows a tiny tray with aggregated counts and a link "Open session replay".
- Right-click kebab offers: ignore-fingerprint (rule), mute-route-for-1h, create-issue, pin-sparkline (promote to dashboard).
- Expand panel has two-state quick-actions: preview (simulate reroute against last 1k requests) and apply (apply policy to live routing). Preview is always safe and non-destructive.
data_model_notes:
What must backend provide per row (minimal):
- time-series vector (48 buckets, counts success/fail)
- fingerprint ids + short label + sample count
- top-3 sample traces (timestamp, short message, request-id)
- route metadata (model version, quantization profile, region)
- simple pre-computed metrics: p50/p95, err%
These are intentionally compact to support cheap list rendering.
heuristics_and_prioritization:
How to rank rows in the table by default:
1) weighted score combining absolute errors in last 24h + delta compared to baseline + severity (5xx > timeout > model-error).
2) user pinned routes always first.
3) Option to switch to 'regression-only' mode (shows top deltas).
Tagging heuristics: group fingerprints if same message AND same top-2 stack frames OR same model-version+token-threshold.
accessibility_considerations: - Sparkline markers must have hover text and keyboard focus equivalent.\n- Color choices must pass contrast for badges; use patterns or dot shapes if colorblind.\n- All quick-actions accessible by keyboard and screen-reader friendly labels.
acceptance_criteria:
MVP acceptance (product + eng):
- List view renders 1000 rows with sparklines without jank on typical SRE machine.
- Expand panel fetches top-3 samples in <300ms.
- Quick-action preview returns simulated reroute metrics within 1s.
- Users can create triage issue with prefilled fingerprint + traces via keyboard-only flow.
- Feature controlled behind a feature-flag and rollout toggle.
backlog_and_next_steps:
Backlog items (ranked):
- [P0] API endpoint: aggregated 48-bucket timeseries + fingerprint map (ENG-1229)
- [P0] Frontend component: tiny sparkline svg with marker overlay (PR: console-prototypes#78)
- [P1] Quick-action preview simulation service (ENG-1344)
- [P1] Create rule modal integration (policy service)
- [P2] Accessibility pass (a11y QA)
- [P3] Dashboard pinning + alert subscription UX
Owner tasks for next week:
- Design: produce hi-fi sprite for 48x12 sparkline and marker hover states (Asha)
- FE: implement basic sparkline component and keyboard nav (Miguel)
- BE: prototype timeseries aggregator endpoint + sample trace fetch (Evan)
open_questions_and_risks:
Open questions:
- How do we dedupe fingerprints across routing fallbacks? (risk: duplicate noise)
- What retention should backend assume for 48-bucket aggregates? (storage/cost tradeoff)
- Preview simulations may leak PII in traces — need scrub rules.
Risks:
- Overloading list with microvisuals could increase cognitive noise; plan to gate behind analytics experiment and gradual rollout.
notes_to_reviewers:
Please review focusing on:
- Are the quick-actions appropriate and safe to expose (preview vs apply)?
- Does the ranking heuristic match on-call workflows?
- Anything missing that would prevent safe rollouts (compliance/audit hooks)?
Add comments inline in the Confluence doc or drop notes in Slack #console-ux.
references_and_inspo: - Example: Datadog sparkline rows, but we favor single-trace quick-preview rather than full flamegraphs.\n- Internal: ties to `failure-replay-and-trace-ux-notes` and `triage-quickstart-canvas` (see linked artifacts).\n- Research: quick look at mental model for sparklines in lists, Nielsen Norman Group notes on microvisualizations.
final_remark: This is intentionally lightweight: target first iteration is 'useful and cheap' rather than exhaustive. If core heuristics and the tiny sparkline give immediate reductions in time-to-detect/triage during the experiment, expand to richer inline diagnostics.
